title: Build Orders
intro: Universal, civ-agnostic build orders. Learn these as templates, then tune them to your civilization's bonuses (shown on each civ page). Openings popularized and explained across the AoE II community — distilled here from t.me/kiritastrich, Spirit of the Law, Hera and CyberDabVinc.

_meta.note: Universal build orders are standard, community-known templates (not verbatim transcripts). They are attributed to the channels that teach them as references. Exact pop/timing numbers are rounded guideposts — adjust by civ, map and patch.

orders.title: Fast Castle (→ Knights or boom)
orders.when: Closed / resource-rich maps (arena-style, or walled Arabia)
orders.goal: Reach Castle Age quickly, then either 2-Stable Knights or drop extra Town Centers to boom.
steps: Eat sheep under the TC, lure both boar, push deer; keep the TC producing villagers non-stop.
Click Feudal Age around 26–28 vils (≈10:30–11:00); build a Barracks + a prerequisite building (Market or Stable) on the way up.
Add Blacksmith during Feudal and click Castle Age immediately (~15:00–16:00).
On Castle: either 2 Stables → Knights, or +2/+3 Town Centers to boom. Get Bloodlines + Husbandry.
tips: Accelerated FC (~20–22 vils) into Scouts + Scorpions + Monks is a strong resource-rich variant (kiritastrich).
Wall while aging if the map is open — an FC build dies to early aggression if scouted.
vils: Dark: 6 food (sheep) → 3 wood → lure boar to food → 4 more wood (7w) → 4 gold → click Feudal ~26–28 pop.
Feudal: send 2 vils to build the prerequisite (Market or Stable) + Blacksmith; hold ~10 food / 10 wood / 4 gold.
Castle (Knights): ~8 gold, ~14 food, rest wood to fund 2 Stables. Castle (boom): push to ~16 wood for +2 Town Centers.

orders.title: Scout Rush (Feudal aggression)
orders.when: Open land maps (Arabia), when you have a stable/cavalry-friendly bonus
orders.goal: Use 4–6 Scout Cavalry to raid villagers and grab map control, then transition.
steps: Click Feudal at ~19–21 pop (~9:30–10:00); build Barracks → Stable immediately.
Queue Scouts continuously; research Bloodlines then armor/forging.
Scout the enemy and send scouts to woodlines/gold; snipe exposed villagers.
Transition: add Archers, or click Castle behind the damage and go Knights.
tips: Don't lose scouts to town-center fire — raid, then retreat.
If walled out, switch to archers or fast Castle instead of forcing scouts.
vils: Dark: 6 food → 3 wood → lure boar → 4 wood (7w) → click Feudal ~20–21 pop.
Feudal: 2 vils build Barracks → Stable; keep ~8 food / 6–8 wood; 2–3 gold for Bloodlines.
Keep food high so Scout production never stops; shift spare vils to wood/gold for the transition.

orders.title: Men-at-Arms → Archers
orders.when: Open land maps; the standard flexible Feudal opener
orders.goal: Apply early M@A pressure, then mass Archers and carry them into Crossbows.
steps: Open with a Barracks; train ~2–3 Militia, upgrade to Men-at-Arms at Feudal (~21–22 pop).
Add 1–2 Archery Ranges; start massing Archers; research Fletching.
Harass with M@A + Archers while scaling; keep villager production high.
Click Castle and upgrade to Crossbows + Bodkin Arrow; add siege or a forward base.
tips: Micro M@A onto woodline/gold villagers, then pull them back as archers arrive.
This is the most universal opener — almost every civ can run a version of it.
vils: Dark: 6 food → 3 wood → 1 vil on Barracks → 4 wood (7w) → 3 gold for Men-at-Arms → click Feudal ~21–22 pop.
Feudal: ~6 wood / 4 gold for 2 Ranges; lean wood to fund Archers, then more gold for Feudal upgrades.
Castle: ~10 wood / 8 gold for Crossbows + Bodkin; add farms for food sustain.

orders.title: Straight Archers (range-first)
orders.when: Open maps when you want clean range pressure without the M@A investment
orders.goal: Mass Feudal archers fast to deny map control and idle the opponent.
steps: Click Feudal ~21–22 pop; build Barracks then 2 Archery Ranges.
Pump Archers; get Fletching and Archer armor; stack to a critical mass (~10–15) before attacking.
Raid wood/gold; force walls and idle time.
Transition to Crossbows in Castle with Bodkin Arrow.
tips: Don't trickle archers in small numbers into TC fire — mass first.
Bring a forward Villager for a tower or forward range if you win the archer fight.
vils: Dark: 6 food → 3 wood → lure boar → 4 wood (7w) → click Feudal ~21–22 pop.
Feudal: heavy wood — ~10–12 wood, ~4 gold, rest food; 2 Ranges pump Archers.
Castle: keep wood high for Crossbows — ~12 wood, ~8 gold, farms for food.

orders.title: Drush (Dark Age Militia rush)
orders.when: Maps where early disruption delays a faster opponent (e.g. vs an FC/boom)
orders.goal: Send 3 Militia in the Dark Age to idle villagers, then follow up (FC or Archers).
steps: Build a Barracks at ~10 pop; queue 3 Militia (skip or delay gold mining via sell/looming).
Send the 3 Militia to the enemy base; attack woodline/gold villagers, then retreat toward home.
Use the bought time to click Feudal cleanly and follow with Archers or a Fast Castle.
Wall your own base so the counter-hit doesn't hurt.
tips: Drush value is in idle time and scouting, not kills — keep the militia alive.
Pairs well with civs that have a strong Militia/infantry line or a fast follow-up.
vils: Dark: 6 food → 3 wood → Barracks at ~10 pop → train 3 Militia → 4 wood (7w) → click Feudal.
After the drush: ~7 wood / 3 gold if going Archers, or pure food/wood for a Fast Castle.
Feudal/Castle: settle into a standard Archer or Fast-Castle allocation.

orders.title: Tower Rush (Trush)
orders.when: Maps where you can deny a key resource (gold/stone/berries) near the enemy
orders.goal: Forward Villagers drop Towers to starve the opponent of resources in Feudal.
steps: Send 4–6 Villagers forward around ~18–20 pop; mine stone on the way.
Drop a Tower on the enemy gold, stone or woodline; tower-watchtower toward your base.
Add more Towers and Archers/Skirmishers to defend them; repair under fire.
Transition behind the resource denial (your opponent is starving).
tips: All-in trushes are risky — keep a fallback economy at home.
Best on civs with tower/building or stone bonuses.
vils: ~18–20 pop: send 4–6 vils forward; 3–4 mine stone on the way; rest stay on food/wood at home.
Forward vils drop Towers; keep 1–2 on stone for follow-ups, rest on wood for repairs and Archers.
Home base: maintain food + wood so you can transition behind the resource denial.

orders.title: Fast Imperial
orders.when: Closed/bowl maps (Arena, Hideout) with a strong unique unit or trebuchet plan
orders.goal: Skip Castle-Age army, rush Imperial Age for Trebuchets / unique units / Bombard Cannons.
steps: Fast Castle with minimal army, then add 2–3 Town Centers and relic/monk value.
Click Imperial Age as soon as affordable (~25:00–28:00).
Hit with Trebuchets + your unique unit / Bombard Cannons before the opponent has Imperial units.
Use stone walls / castles to stay safe while you tech.
tips: Vulnerable to early aggression — wall and scout.
Strong on civs with a dominant unique unit or gunpowder.
vils: Dark→Castle: Fast-Castle split (6f / 7w / 4g → click up); add 2–3 Town Centers in Castle.
Castle: ~16 wood / 8 food / 6 gold; grab relics with a Monk; keep booming villagers.
Imperial: rebalance to gold + wood for Trebuchets / unique unit / Bombard Cannon.

orders.title: Boom (multiple Town Centers)
orders.when: When you've secured the map or play a closed/economic civ
orders.goal: Scale to 100+ villagers via extra Town Centers for a decisive late-game economy.
steps: Reach Castle Age, then immediately place 2–3 additional Town Centers on wood/gold/stone.
Produce villagers from ALL Town Centers constantly; never let any idle.
Rebalance to ~40% wood to fund farms, military buildings and siege.
Add army + upgrades as the economy comes online; defend with walls/TCs.
tips: A boom only wins if you convert the economy into army before you're overrun.
Pair with a fast-Imperial or heavy-siege plan for a powerful late game.
vils: Castle Age: drop 2–3 extra Town Centers on wood/gold/stone; train villagers from EVERY TC constantly.
Rebalance toward ~40% wood to fund farms, military buildings and siege.
Late game: ~30+ on food (farms), ~20 wood, ~10 gold, rest per army; aim for 100+ villagers.
